description: freshness.v2 §2.5, a subscriber's rule for a heartbeat. Written by an independent reading of the text (Python, standard library), checked, never blessed. Each case names a layout of the core's `spec/conformance/heartbeat/layouts.json` and the collections the subscriber `follows`, by resource, then its `steps` in order, each at `at`, the subscriber's monotonic clock in milliseconds. `put` and `delete`: a mutation of `key` it heard, with its in-band `stamp` (`run_width` 16 or 32, `run`, `seq`) or `null` for none; a put older than the one held within one run is not taken. `read`: a complete read's answer of `collection`, asked at `asked` and arrived at `at`, its `live` members each with its stamp: it replaces the collection, merged with what was heard from `asked` on (within one run the higher seq kept, across two runs the answer's). `heartbeat`: CH's `tag`, the heartbeat key's `stamp` and the `body` in hex, then `expect`: `{revision: true}` (the tag is not the layout's), `{refused: token}` (core §7.5's body refusals), `{older: true}` (within one run, a seq not after the last read heartbeat's by serial order), or `{read: {gap, sections}}`, `gap` true when the seq is not the last read one's plus 1 within one run, and each collection, by resource, `not_followed`, `absent` (its map bit 0), `diverged` (its digest or live count not the view's), or `{confirmed: [keys]}`, the members vouched for, in key order. A heartbeat expected `revision`, `refused` or `older` is not counted: it moves neither the sequence nor a count of divergences in a row. `check`: the collections due a read (`reread_due`, two divergences in a row, in map order), whether the last heartbeat read followed a gap (`gap`), and each named key's last heartbeat confirmation (`confirmed`, its `at`, or `null`: none since its last mutation, or not held). Cases with a `catalog` are §2.5's rule for an owner heartbeat, written by an independent reading of the text and checked by a second, never blessed. `catalog` is the catalog the owner names, which the subscriber holds: the layouts its entries name, in index order, an entry `{iface, contract}` naming a revision of `iface` that is no layout's; or `null` where the owner names none. `follows` gives, per layout, the collections the subscriber follows of that interface, and it holds those layouts' revisions alone. A collection's class is `link` where its resolved `link.exposure` reads `link` in the layout's contract, and `host` otherwise. A `read` names its `layout`, and a `heartbeat` the `layout` it covers. `owner_heartbeat`: the key's `class`, CH's `tag`, the key's `stamp` and the `body` in hex, then `expect`: `{refused: token}` (core §7.5 refuses it whole: `tag`, `short`, `code`, `order`, `leb128`, `trailing`, `pad`), `{older: true}`, or `{read: {gap, groups}}`: `gap` true when the seq is not the last read owner heartbeat's plus 1 on that key within one run, and each group in order, its `index` and one of `refused` (`unknown_catalog` or `unknown_index`, or core §7.5's token for its sections), `not_followed: true`, `revision: true`, or `sections`: each collection of its interface, by resource, `not_followed`, `other_class` (not of the key's class, whatever its map bit), `absent`, `diverged` or `{confirmed: [keys]}`. An owner heartbeat expected `refused` or `older` is not counted; a group that is `refused`, `not_followed` or `revision` moves no count of divergences. `check`: `reread_due` by layout, a layout with none left out; `gap` by key, the class or the covered interface's layout, for each key one has been read on: whether the last one read on that key followed a gap; `lost`, by layout, the followed collections read as lost deliveries, a layout with none left out; and `confirmed`, as above.

cases.note: a section whose digest is the view's confirms each member vouched for, at the heartbeat's arrival; a cleared bit confirms nothing of its member, which keeps its last confirmation
a missed put: the collection's digest is not the view's, so nothing is confirmed there, the others still are; two in a row make it due a read
a divergence, then a map bit of 0, then a divergence: not two in a row, so not due a read
a read's answer replaces the view: a member it left out leaves it, and the next heartbeat confirms what the owner holds
what the reader heard after it asked is merged with the answer, as a late joiner's seed is: within one run the higher seq is kept, across two runs the answer's value stands
a delete heard after the read was asked is kept over the answer's older value of its run, and its member leaves the digest

a gap in the heartbeat key's seqs is a heartbeat lost, until one arrives in sequence; another run starts the sequence again, a 32-bit run 9 and a 16-bit run 9 two runs; the seq wraps in serial order, 2^24 - 1 then 0 in sequence
within one run, a heartbeat whose seq is not after the last one's confirms nothing and is not counted: the same seq, an earlier one, and one 2^23 ahead, unordered
another revision's tag confirms nothing, and a refused body neither; neither moves the sequence
a templated section as a list: nine live members, one vouched for
a live member the view holds with no in-band stamp has no digest, so its collection diverges
a put older than the one held within its run is not taken; one of another run is; a deleted member leaves the digest
a collection the view does not follow is not read, and its divergence makes no read due
a time unknown, all 42 bits set, is read as any other heartbeat

a heartbeat stopped at the tag, the body or the order is not counted: 5 read, a refused 6, then 7 follows a gap; a divergence, another revision's tag, then a divergence are two read in a row, so a read is due

W2's three interfaces in one owner heartbeat of the class `host`: a group per interface, each read as a heartbeat covering its interface would be, its members confirmed at the owner heartbeat's arrival; in the next, a cleared bit in vital.v1's group and one in alert.v1's confirm nothing of their members, which keep their last confirmation

a gap in the owner heartbeat key's seqs is an owner heartbeat lost for every interface it covers at once: every collection of the key's class, in each interface a group on the key has named, is read as a lost delivery until an owner heartbeat arrives in sequence; the one after the gap still confirms; another run starts the sequence again

within one run, an owner heartbeat whose seq is not after the last read one's on its key confirms nothing, for any group, and is not counted: the same seq, an earlier one, and one 2^23 ahead, unordered; the next in sequence follows no gap

an unknown index beside known ones: the catalog holds indices 0 to 2 and 4 is past it, so with a catalog of five entries a group of index 7 is refused, and that group alone: the groups before it are read, and so would one after it be

the catalog the owner names holds three entries, and the last group's index is 4: refused, so vital.v1's member is not confirmed, and the two groups before it are; the owner heartbeat is read, and counted
the owner names no catalog: every group's index is refused, `unknown_catalog`, and nothing is confirmed; the owner heartbeat is still a read one, so the next follows no gap

a divergence in one group: the reader missed knob.v1's second put, so that group's section diverges and confirms nothing, and the groups beside it confirm; two in a row make that collection alone due a read, whose answer replaces it, and the next owner heartbeat confirms it

a group stopped before its sections are read is not counted, and takes nothing from the groups beside it: knob.v1's group diverges, then carries another revision's tag, then a bit after its last field, and no read is due; then it diverges again, two read in a row for that collection, so a read is due, while alert.v1's group, a live count above its cardinality, is refused alone; every owner heartbeat here is a read one, so none follows a gap

an owner heartbeat that core §7.5 refuses whole confirms nothing for any group and is not counted: an index twice, CH's tag not 0, a pad bit set; none moves the sequence, so seq 4 after seq 0 follows a gap

two classes, two keys, two sequences: mixed.v1's `link` collections ride the `link` key's group and its `host` collection the `host` key's, beside vital.v1's; each key counts its own seqs, so a gap on the `link` key reads mixed.v1's two `link` collections as lost deliveries and says nothing of the `host` key's

a collection of the other class is not read on a key, whatever its map bit says: a `link` owner heartbeat whose group marks mixed.v1's `host` collection, its digest the view's, confirms none of its members; a divergence there is not counted either; `uplink`'s map bit is 0, absent
a reader bound to one interface holds its revision alone: it skips the groups of the others by their sizes, their sections unread, here bits no revision would accept, and reads its own

both forms from one owner, an interface on each: hb.v1 by its own heartbeat, vital.v1 by the `host` owner heartbeat; each key is a sequence of its own, so a gap in hb.v1's heartbeats says nothing of vital.v1

an owner heartbeat with no group for an interface, as a standby's is left out, confirms nothing of it, loses nothing, and is not counted for its collections: knob.v1's group diverges, is left out twice, and diverges again: two in a row, so a read is due

the collections a key covers are those of each interface a group on it has named within the run, the group read after the gap among them: vital.v1's group first comes in the owner heartbeat that follows the gap, and its collection is read as a lost delivery with the others

another revision by the catalog's word: the group's index names a revision of vital.v1 that is not the one the reader holds, though its tag is the same, 8: the group confirms nothing, and the groups before it do
the time unknown, all 42 bits set, under a 32-bit run: read as any other owner heartbeat
